 Despite being behind first choice striker Samu in the pecking order, the Mexican striker has impressed for the “azuis e brancos”.

Update: Nov 6th, 2026 12:50 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google It will come as no surprise that the three ‘grandes’ lead the way in the current Liga Portugal standings. What is noteworthy however is that table topping FC Porto have a 100% record with ten wins from ten games. 
 The side from the north of the country have found their groove under new coach Francesco Farioli and under the Italian last season, FC Porto claimed their first league title since 2022.
 Entre subidas 📈 e descidas 📉, a tabela da #LigaPortugalBetclic não para!
Que lugar ocupa a tua equipa? pic.twitter.com/9YIrKrPbux 
— Liga Portugal (@ligaportugal) November 3, 2026 
 Porto currently lead bitter rivals Benfica by five points and in their ten games in the 2026-27 season, have only shipped four goals in the process, scoring 25.
 Despite only getting three outings for the team in the domestic league, Santi Gimenez has impressed bagging his only goal of the league in a 1-4 win away at Casa Pia. 
 𝚁𝚞𝚗𝚗𝚒𝚗𝚐 𝚝𝚘 💨 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐚̃𝐞𝐬 ⚽
Está a chegar mais um 𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐲 𝐝𝐚𝐲 fundamental ⚡️ #VSCFCP pic.twitter.com/Se0pWiy3Pn 
— FC Porto (@FCPorto) November 6, 2026 
 The Mexican is mainly being used as a high impact sub by coach Faroli and remains as a solid backup solution to key striker Samu Omorodion. 
 With Gimenez arriving late in the window on loan from AC Milan and coming back to full fitness after his ankle injury, the Porto coaching staff have managed his workload carefully, using him primarily as a high-impact second-half option rather than rushing him into heavy 90-minute starter loads.
 FC Porto's Santiago Gimenez JOSE COELHO Record in sight
 Under manager André Villas-Boas back in the 2010-11 season, Porto mounted a 16-game winning streak in the league during their legendary unbeaten campaign, on their way to winning the domestic title and Europa League treble.
 The ‘Dragoes’ face a major test this weekend as they face Vitoria de Guimaraes on Sunday, with the Estádio D. Afonso Henriques one of Portugal football’s more tricky away days.
